items.markingKey: (c) Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, because employment of children below 14 is prohibited.
options: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012

items.stem: Give a reason for the following: The JJ Act has a separate body for children in need of care and protection.
items.answer: Such children have not committed any offence and need care, shelter and rehabilitation, not a trial.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: Such children have not committed any offence and need care, shelter and rehabilitation, not a trial. (1 mark for the reason, 1 for linking it to the statement).

items.stem: "The POCSO Act provides special courts." Examine this statement with reference to constitutional provisions and laws for children.
items.answer: The statement is valid. Trials involving child victims need to be quick and child-friendly to avoid further trauma.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (trials involving child victims need to be quick and child-friendly to avoid further trauma.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem: The following statement about the child and child rights is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "The UNCRC defines a child as a person below 14 years."
items.answer: The UNCRC defines a child as a person below 18 years.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (The UNCRC defines a child as a person below 18 years.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about constitutional provisions and laws for children:
I. The 2016 amendment renamed the law the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act.
II. The POCSO Act was amended in 2019 to increase punishments, including the death penalty for aggravated penetrative sexual assault.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.

items.stem: Fatima, aged 17, is accused of a heinous offence, and the Board after preliminary assessment finds that the accused should be tried as an adult. Which body or court will deal with this? Give a reason for your answer.
items.answer: Children's Court; the case is transferred to the Children's Court after the preliminary assessment.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 for Children's Court, 1 for the reason (the case is transferred to the Children's Court after the preliminary assessment).

items.stem: What is meant by 'child labour' in the context of constitutional provisions and laws for children?
items.answer: Work that deprives children of their childhood and education and harms their development; employment of children below 14 is banned.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: child labour correctly explained as work that deprives children of their childhood and education and harms their development; employment of children below 14 is banned.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about the child and child rights:
I. Countries that are party to the UNCRC report to the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child.
II. The NCPCR monitors whether laws and policies protect child rights in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 and answer the questions that follow.
"No child in conflict with law can be sentenced to death or to life imprisonment without the possibility of release. The Act deals with two groups of children: those in conflict with law and those in need of care and protection. The JJ Act, 2015 replaced the Juvenile Justice Act of 2000."
(i) Adoption in India is regulated by the: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'child in conflict with law' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The JJ Act has a separate body for children in need of care and protection. (1)
items.answer: (i) Central Adoption Resource Authority (ii) A child who is alleged or found to have committed an offence and is below 18 years on the date of the offence. (iii) Such children have not committed any offence and need care, shelter and rehabilitation, not a trial.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) Central Adoption Resource Authority (ii) A child who is alleged or found to have committed an offence and is below 18 years on the date of the offence. (iii) Such children have not committed any offence and need care, shelter and rehabilitation, not a trial.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The POCSO Act provides special courts.
Reason (R): Trials involving child victims need to be quick and child-friendly to avoid further trauma.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both are true and R explains A: trials involving child victims need to be quick and child-friendly to avoid further trauma.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015:
I. A child in conflict with law can be sentenced to death.
II. No child in conflict with law can be sentenced to death or to life imprisonment without the possibility of release.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: II only
items.markingKey: (b) I is incorrect: The JJ Act prohibits death sentence and life imprisonment without the possibility of release for children. II is correct.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about constitutional provisions and laws for children:
I. The POCSO Act was amended in 2019 to increase punishments, including the death penalty for aggravated penetrative sexual assault.
II. The 2016 amendment renamed the law the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act.
III. The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 fixes the marriageable age at 18 for females and 21 for males.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: All of them
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct. III is correct.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the child and child rights and answer the questions that follow.
"Countries that are party to the UNCRC report to the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child. The four guiding principles of the UNCRC are non-discrimination, best interests of the child, the right to life, survival and development, and respect for the views of the child. Child rights are often grouped as rights to survival, development, protection and participation."
(i) The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child was adopted in: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'UNCRC' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The best interests of the child guide courts in custody cases. (1)
items.answer: (i) 1989 (ii) The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, adopted by the UN General Assembly on 20 November 1989. (iii) The UNCRC and Indian law make the child's welfare the primary consideration in decisions about children.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) 1989 (ii) The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, adopted by the UN General Assembly on 20 November 1989. (iii) The UNCRC and Indian law make the child's welfare the primary consideration in decisions about children.

items.stem: The parents of a 15-year-old girl arrange her marriage. Which law applies? Give a reason for your answer.
items.answer: Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006; it fixes the marriageable age at 18 for females and 21 for males.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 for Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, 1 for the reason (it fixes the marriageable age at 18 for females and 21 for males).

items.stem: Which term describes the following? A child who is, for example, homeless, abandoned, orphaned, abused or at risk, and needs care.
items.answer: child in need of care and protection
items.markingKey: (a) child in need of care and protection: a child who is, for example, homeless, abandoned, orphaned, abused or at risk, and needs care.
options: child in need of care and protection

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"A Juvenile Justice Board has a Metropolitan or Judicial Magistrate and two social workers, at least one of whom is a woman. Offences are classified as petty, serious and heinous under the Act. The JJ Act, 2015 replaced the Juvenile Justice Act of 2000. The 2021 amendment empowered District Magistrates to issue adoption orders."
(i) Explain the term 'Juvenile Justice Board', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: The Juvenile Justice Board includes social workers. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "Every child accused of any offence is tried as an adult." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (1)
items.answer: (i) The body that deals with children in conflict with law, consisting of a magistrate and two social workers, at least one a woman. (ii) The aim of the juvenile system is reform and rehabilitation rather than only punishment. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Only a child of 16-18 accused of a heinous offence may be tried as an adult, after preliminary assessment.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) The body that deals with children in conflict with law, consisting of a magistrate and two social workers, at least one a woman. (ii) The aim of the juvenile system is reform and rehabilitation rather than only punishment. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Only a child of 16-18 accused of a heinous offence may be tried as an adult, after preliminary assessment.

items.stem:
Arrange the following in chronological order (earliest first):
I. The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act
II. The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
III. The 86th Amendment inserts Article 21A
IV. India becomes a party to the UNCRC
items.answer: I, IV, III, II
items.markingKey: (a) The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act (1986); India becomes a party to the UNCRC (1992); The 86th Amendment inserts Article 21A (2002); The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (2012).
